When r = 1 , M (1 , L, c 2 ) is isomorphic to S [ c 2 ] , the Hilbert scheme of 0 -dimensional closed subschemes in S of length c 2 . Fogarty showed that S [ n ] ( n ∈ Z ≥ 0 ) is a smooth projective variety of dimension 2 n [Fog68] and computed its Picard group [Fog73]. The Betti numbers of S [ n ] were completely determined by Göttsche [G ¨ 90]. When r ≥ 2 , M ( r, L, c 2 ) can be reducible or non-reduced. But starting from Donaldson's generic smoothness result [Don90], the study of M ( r, L, c 2 ) has revealed that M ( r, L, c 2 ) has better geometric properties as we fix r ≥ 2 , L , and let c 2 increase. For example, when c 2 is large enough, Gieseker-Li [GL94] [GL96] and O'Grady [O'G96] showed that M ( r, L, c 2 ) is irreducible, normal, and generically smooth of expected dimension. Some asymptotic phenomena also occur in the Picard group and Betti numbers of M ( r, L, c 2 ) ( r ≥ 2 ) [Qin92][Li96][Li97][CW22].

This raises a natural question:

Question 1.1. Are there asymptotic phenomena similar to those above in the geometry of M ( r, L, c 2 ) when r = 0 ?

Sheaves on S of rank zero are supported on points or curves. In this paper, we focus on those pure sheaves supported on curves, which are called one-dimensional sheaves. In contrast to the positive rank case, there are few general results for the moduli space of one-dimensional sheaves. An essential difficulty is that the supports of one-dimensional sheaves can be singular, even non-reduced. To distinguish this case, we use the following notation. Given a nonzero effective divisor β on S and an integer χ , denote by M β,χ the moduli space parametrizing polystable one-dimensional sheaves F on S , with determinant det( F ) ∼ = O S ( β ) and Euler characteristic χ ( F ) = χ . We will make the following assumption on β , unless otherwise stated.

## Assumption 1.2. The following conditions hold:

- (1) β is base-point-free.
- (2) A general curve in | β | is smooth and connected.

Aconjecture [SZ24, Conjecture 1.3] was proposed on the stabilization of (intersection cohomology) Betti numbers of M β,χ when χ is fixed and β is sufficiently positive, as an analogue of [CW22, Conjecture 1.1]. When S is a del Pezzo surface, this conjecture was resolved in [PSSZ24] by proving an asymptotic formula of the refined BPS invariants which also refine the Betti numbers.

The primary motivation of this paper is to explore the stabilization of the Picard number ρ ( M β,χ ) of M β,χ when β is sufficiently positive. Here, the Picard number ρ ( X ) of a proper scheme X is defined as the dimension of the Q -vector space Num Q ( X ) of the numerically equivalence classes of line bundles on X with rational coefficients, in the sense of [Kle66]. Fix a basis [ L i ] ( i = 1 , · · · , ρ ( S )) for Num Q ( S ) , where each L i is a smooth, connected effective divisor. We specify a positivity condition for β as follows.

## Definition 1.3. We say a divisor β on S satisfies (P) if

- (1) β satisfies Assumption 1.2.
- (2) The arithmetic genus p a ( β ) > 0 .
- (3) For each 1 ≤ i ≤ ρ ( S ) , there exists a smooth and connected curve L ′ i ∈ | β -L i | such that L i meets L ′ i transversally with intersection number L i · L ′ i ≥ | χ | +1 .

Note that for an ample divisor β , the multiple nβ satisfies (P) for all n ≫ 0 .

Our first main result is the following. We obtain an asymptotic lower bound of the Picard number of M β,χ .
